title: 1945 fire Farmers Co-op
description: On May 12, 1945, a devastating fire reduced the three-storey brick building owned by the United Farmers Store to a gaunt shell of blackened walls. As one of Hartland’s leading general stores, its loss was deeply felt, with damages estimated at up to $20,000. The blaze also destroyed the offices on the second floor of Fred Boyd, the town magistrate, as well as those of R. D. Stewart and G. R. McCutcheon. The building, owned by a stock company of local farmers led by President William Bubar, had only recently been purchased after years of renting. Frank Plummer managed the store at the time. Thanks to the swift response of the town’s fire brigade, the fire was contained before reinforcements from Bristol and Woodstock arrived. Neighboring businesses, Hartland Clothing Company to the south and Plummer’s Store to the north, suffered only minor water damage, as their stock and ledgers had been removed as a precaution.
